fichas.title: Station Buildings
fichas.summary: Station buildings connect the railway network with other modes of transport. Railway-operated services are generally limited to ticket sales, information and luggage care; other services and shops may be operated by leaseholders.
uses: Connect rail transport to other transport modes
Provide ticket sales, information and luggage services

fichas.title: TravelCentre
fichas.summary: The TravelCentre provides personal advice and ticket sales. Its modular fitting-out system uses a metre grid; adjustable legs accommodate installation conditions and the height difference between seated staff and standing passengers. Waiting customers need sufficient space and a clear area in front of the counter; where there are multiple counters, a centralised queue is recommended. Ticket machines can reduce counter workload.

fichas.title: ServicePoint
fichas.summary: The ServicePoint is a direct contact point for travellers and a central information interface between customers and station staff. Three types are described: a free-standing singular unit, an integrated unit, and a mobile rolling stand. Sizes are given for example workplace configurations; the text notes that the mobile type dimensions are still at the design stage and may change.

fichas.title: Station Stairs and Escalators
fichas.summary: Usable stair width should be a multiple of the walking passage width and at least the stated clear minimum. Stair width may also be determined from expected peak passenger numbers using the printed formula and parameters. Provide waiting space in front of stairs, contrasting strips on steps, and escalators above the stated passenger thresholds or for the stated level difference. The escalator minimum width accommodates luggage trolleys.

RAILWAYS
Station Buildings

Station buildings (German Railways uses the term reception
buildings) serve to connect the railway network to other means of
transport. The services offered in-house by the railway company
are limited to essentials like sales of tickets and tours, information
and taking care of luggage. Other services and shops are operated
by leaseholders in the station area -----> 0-

e.

TraveiCentre
The TraveiCentre is for personal advice and the sale of tickets.
The fitting out is modular on a metre grid, and the smallest unit, a
counter, is 2 m x 3 m. The elements are delivered completely preinstalled. The adjustable legs enable adaptation of the installation
and compensation for the height difference between the seated
staff and the standing passengers. The system can be completed
with various supplementary elements ----->

e.

0

A sufficiently large area should be provided for waiting customers
with a free space in front of the counter. If there is more than
one counter, organise one centralised queue if possible. Ticket
machines are also provided to relieve the workload at the
counter----->

e.

Dimensions of free-standing ticket

machine; can also be installed.

1. Singular type ServicePoint: free-standing in the reception building,
various sizes, modular, different layouts for 1---4 employees (for
two workplaces LWH: 3.00 m x 5.00 m x 3.50 m).
2. Integrated type ServicePoint: within a fagade or inside the
station building, adjacent to the TraveiCentre, for 1---4 employees
(LWH: 2.00 m x 2.60 m x 3.10 m for one workplace, with each
further workplace elongating the fixture by 1.70 m.)
3. Mobile type ServicePoint: a rolling stand for flexible use in
the station building and also on platforms, for one employee
each (LHB: 0.90 m x 0.80 m x 2.30 m). These sizes are at the
design stage and could still alter.

Stairs
The usable stair width should be a multiple of 80 em (walking
passage width) but at least 2.40 m clear. The stair width can also
be determined from the expected passenger numbers according
to the formula:

=0.65
=1.0
=120-180s
=0.80 m
=0.60 m

Stair dimensions, see-----> p. 120 ff. The waiting space in front of the
stairs should be 1.5 times the stair width. The first and last steps
must, and all other steps should, be provided with a 6 em wide
contrasting strip.

Escalators
From a passenger density of more than 3000 people per hour or,
with a difference in levels of 8 m, more than 500 people, escalators
should be provided. The minimum width should be 1 m in order to
be able to transport luggage trolleys -----> p. 126 ff.
